d13-007.note: SLA: the definition of an unavailable hosted zone and the credit table are facts; the SLA page states its commitment only through the credit table, so there is no single 'availability percentage' sentence.

d13-015.note: Alias to another record: the guide states only 'another record in the same hosted zone' (route53-alias-to-record-in-zone-uses-target-ttl, route53-alias-target-another-record-all-types-except-ns-soa); registrar search for other-zone wording found nothing. Do not claim that an alias can or cannot target another hosted zone.

d13-017.note: The alias vs CNAME comparison has no health check row; Evaluate Target Health is covered by route53-alias-to-aws-use-evaluate-target-health-not-health-check and route53-failover-alias-health-check-and-evaluate-both-true.

d13-020.note: The CloudFront alias hosted zone ID (Z2FDTNDATAQYW2) stands only in the full guide indexes of the AWS General Reference and the CloudFormation guide (no saved page snapshot); not exam material, not mined. CloudFront alias facts: alternate domain name, two records for IPv6, public hosted zones only.

d13-022.note: No sentence says an alias cannot target an EC2 instance; the alias target list has no EC2 entry and the EC2 page routes with an A record and an Elastic IP address. Write 'use an A record with an Elastic IP address', never 'alias cannot point to EC2'.

d13-032.note: No sentence says the lowest-latency Region can differ from the nearest one; use route53-latency-data-is-aws-traffic-not-your-resources and route53-latency-changes-over-time instead.

d13-040.note: No sentence says the primary failover record must have a health check; the guide says a health check on the secondary is optional (route53-failover-secondary-health-check-optional) and describes the responses when both have one (route53-failover-both-unhealthy-returns-primary).

d13-045.note: The guide never says canary or blue/green; it says weighted routing is useful for testing new versions of software (route53-choose-weighted-routing-proportions, route53-weighted-routing-purpose).

d13-067.note: The Route 53 vs Global Accelerator comparison facts stay in the route53 namespace with an explicit scope; chapter 15 has its own Global Accelerator facts on the same FAQ sentences.

d13-072.note: No sentence states that VPCs in several Regions can be associated with one private hosted zone; the FAQ says answers are available in every associated VPC and VPCs in different Regions need connectivity (route53-faq-phz-across-regions-needs-connectivity).

d13-080.note: The hybrid DNS whitepaper (marked historical) gives a selection table, not a recommendation sentence; its 'no logging' limitation is outdated (route53-hybrid-whitepaper-logging-reason-outdated).

d13-082.note: No page gives a rename date; the Global Resolver preview post (2025-11-30) announces the rename (route53-change-vpc-resolver-rename-2025-11).

d13-097.note: AWS pages describe DNSSEC signing for public hosted zones only; no sentence about private hosted zones (registrar search of the guide, FAQ and pricing found none). Do not state that private zones cannot be signed.

d13-112.note: The 2025-11-19 post covers API requests (control plane) over PrivateLink; it says nothing about how DNS queries are answered.

d13-119.note: The pages name the condition key route53:VPCs and say creating a private hosted zone needs EC2 permissions; no quotable list of the IAM actions for VPC association (registrar search for route53:AssociateVPCWithHostedZone found none).
